features.name: Phone login, OTP and sign-in doors
rules: One door per phone state: an account is new, ready, under review, rejected or deactivated — the router shows exactly that door.
OTP entry copy is a test contract (auth.verifyOtp / auth.enterCode), EN + UR.

evidence.proves: Each sign-in door routes correctly and OTP resume works on a real browser against QA.
Door selection and login-window logic are locked by unit guards.

The pre-authentication account lookup stopped handing out the account. `lookup_user_by_phone` is anon-callable by design (0149) because checkPhoneRegistration asks it before a code is sent, and it answered with 21 fields; the read-set was rebuilt caller by caller from the three call sites it had in src/lib/auth.ts — checkPhoneRegistration consumes `is_active` and `role`, the post-OTP profile read and resumeSession run with a session already in hand and build the session user through userFromRow. 0201 scopes the answer to the identity the caller has PROVED: `public.app_current_user_id() IS DISTINCT FROM users.id` returns only `{is_active, role}`, the account's own authenticated session gets the full row unchanged, and NULL still means no account. Deactivation is still decided from `is_active` before any session is minted, and the ACL is untouched (anon + authenticated + PUBLIC default, exactly the deployed catalogs). Non-vacuous: the captured deployed body is applied first on the same fixture and asserted to expose photo_url, job_title, tenant_id, membership_role and branch_scope to an anonymous caller. The one client change this required — the fourth call site, added by this change — is in the demo bridge: demo mode cannot open a session from phone OTP, so its lookup ran before any session existed, and the profile is re-read once the session is. It is gated on the door answer carrying no `id` (the full row always has one, it is the primary key), so the condition is the signal itself rather than the mode, and any future pre-session read is covered by it; live mode reaches that point with the session verifyOtp just opened, where the re-read is a no-op. 22/22 PASS in tests/unit/preAuthRequestPrivacy.test.ts.
evidence.where: tests/unit/preAuthRequestPrivacy.test.ts (22/22, PGlite + two lineages), supabase/migrations/0201_the_pre_login_lookup_answers_for_the_number_only.sql, src/lib/auth.ts, backups/def-lookup_user_by_phone.sql, tests/unit/loginDoor.test.ts

evidence.proves: 0201 also replaces this function's body on a lineage that cannot support the deployed one, so it was proved against both rather than replayed and assumed. Measured: production has no `canonical_phone(text)`, no `resolve_active_shop(uuid)` and no `memberships` table, and carries an older 14-field body of this same function — naming any of those unguarded would raise `function public.canonical_phone(text) does not exist` at the first call there, which a create-time replay cannot detect because PL/pgSQL resolves references at execution (the trap 0200 hit). Every reference one lineage lacks now sits in its own branch behind `to_regprocedure` / `to_regclass`; the full answer is built from the `users` columns both lineages have, verified column by column. A second PGlite fixture with production's 18-column `users` and no memberships proves it: the captured deployed body is asserted to FAIL there, and the ledger's body answers `{is_active, role}` anonymously and the full row for the account itself, with no membership keys and no error. Baseline replay: 0201 PASS on staging and PASS on production.
evidence.where: tests/unit/preAuthRequestPrivacy.test.ts (older-lineage block), npm run verify:baseline -- --baseline production|staging --files supabase/migrations/0201_…, backups/backup-production-gkswcfljxlutkfdvvqng-2026-10-01T11-21-48.sql

evidence.proves: The minimized answer was verified against the LIVE QA database after 0200/0201 were applied there in the authorized 2026-10-13 window, not only against PGlite: read-only through anon (key sets only, no PII printed), `lookup_user_by_phone` answers an unauthenticated caller with exactly `[is_active, role]`; the account's own authenticated session still receives the full 21-key profile row with every field `userFromRow` consumes (id, name, phone, role, is_active, tenant_id), and the same session asking about a different number receives only `[is_active, role]` — scoping is per proved identity, not per session (5/5 PASS). The ledger that carries the body agrees byte-for-byte (verify PASS — 193 files, newest 0201, target project bpybjrjenwccowvtrevu). The previously-blocked lanes then ran against the migrated schema: accountDeletion PASS, employeePermissions PASS (38/48 tests); the two reds are pre-existing and documented — employeeInviteLifecycle (`ROLE_NOT_FOUND_OR_NOT_AUTHORIZED`, the category `docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md` §8.6 already records) and tenantResolverReplay (`current_branch_scope` re-derives the active shop; open finding S3/C2 of `RBAC_BRANCH_SCOPE_AUDIT.md`). 0200 defines only `public.get_my_shop_request` and 0201 only `public.lookup_user_by_phone`; neither names a resolver, so neither red can be this change's.

risks: The OTP copy is asserted by E2E: changing it without updating the lane turns otpResume red.

FIXED at the database boundary by 0201: this lookup used to answer any caller with the whole account (21 fields — employment record, lifecycle stamps, photo URL, tenant and membership context) while the pre-session consumer read two of them. It now answers the door question only — whether the account is open and its role — unless the caller is authenticated AS the account being looked up, in which case the full row comes back exactly as before. What remains, by design: a caller who knows a number can still learn that it has an account and which role, because that IS the door's question. Demo mode re-reads the profile after its session bridge (src/lib/auth.ts), which is what keeps a demoed sign-in from building a session out of the door answer.

features.name: PIN and biometric re-entry
rules: PIN and biometric are a device-local convenience only; the Supabase session is still the authority.
A stolen device must not yield the DB without the PIN/biometric gate.

evidence.proves: PIN hashing/lockout and biometric availability handling behave as specified.

The browser ceremony is one a real authenticator answers: enrolment records the credential's key, a real assertion verifies against it, a tampered signature is refused, the PIN screen asks for the enrolled credential, and an origin that cannot host WebAuthn (an IP literal) is named rather than blamed on the phone.

risks: The native plugin path (the APK's OS prompt) has no automated lane: a CDP virtual authenticator covers WebAuthn only, so the APK half is verified by unit contract and by hand on a device.
Fingerprint enrolment is impossible on an IP-literal origin, by WebAuthn's own rule: the app now says so (reason no_domain_origin) instead of offering a control that cannot work.

features.name: Owner registration and shop requests
rules: A shop request is never self-approved: it enters through registration and is approved by the super-admin.
Phone formatting/validation is shared (src/lib/phoneInput.ts), not re-implemented per screen.

The applicant never reads shop_requests directly — the table is RLS-protected with no client policy, so both the sign-in gate and the register screens read it through `get_my_shop_request`, which therefore has to stay executable by `anon` as well as `authenticated`. Measured read-only on the deployed catalogs: PUBLIC, anon and authenticated all hold EXECUTE. The guard's PRE_AUTH_RPCS entry fails if a migration ever clears anon from it.

The pre-login answer carries the fields the pre-login screens render and nothing else — no identity-document URL, no coordinates, no registry number, no premise, no reviewer. Widening that list is a decision about what an unauthenticated caller may see, so it changes tests/unit/preAuthRequestPrivacy.test.ts with it (0200).

evidence.proves: Registration-to-approval path is exercised in a browser; phone/invite rules are unit-locked.

SUPERSEDED BY 0200, kept for provenance: the ACL measurement below still stands and is now asserted through the ledger's own statements, but its conclusion that this function should stay a documented ledger gap is retired — the ledger is no longer silent about the function, so LEDGER_GAPS is empty and the name is checked like any other. The shop-request read path is anon-callable BY DESIGN, and now enforced rather than assumed. `get_my_shop_request` is a SECURITY DEFINER function that returns the request matching the phone it is handed (found:false when none); checkPhoneRegistration asks before a code is sent and the register screens read the request they just submitted, so both pre-session callers need it as anon. Its CREATE predates the adopted ledger (the definition was captured read-only as backups/def-get_my_shop_request.sql; 0177 pins its search_path, so the committed ledger itself assumes it), which is why it is recorded as an evidenced ledger gap instead of a grant. Its ACL was measured read-only on the deployed catalogs on 2026-10-13 — {=X/public, postgres=X, anon=X, authenticated=X}, with lookup_user_by_phone and delete_branch as controls whose grants the ledger states and the probe reproduced — so the effective permissions are the intended ones and no migration is warranted. The same probe let the ledger fold be checked against reality for five other functions (5/5 agreement), and exposed a modelling bug the fold had (a statement naming PUBLIC, anon and authenticated applied only the first role it matched) that had hidden two lanes calling the revoked void_sale_v1.

The pre-login answer stopped carrying the application row. 0200 projects `get_my_shop_request` to the nine fields the pre-login screens render (id, status, rejection_reason, owner_name, owner_phone, shop_name, shop_type, created_at, updated_at) and no longer ships the applicant's CNIC front/back and business-licence URLs, the shop's exact coordinates, the registry number, the premise or the reviewer. What was measured before the change: the deployed body ran `SELECT row_to_json(sr)` — the whole row — the deployed row is 23 columns, the only pre-login consumer (RegisterStatusPage) renders five of them, and the client type requires two more; of the deployed requests, one existed, none carried a document URL and one carried coordinates, so the document exposure was potential while the coordinate exposure was actual. The ACL is deliberately unchanged (PUBLIC + anon + authenticated, exactly the measured catalogs; service_role still reaches it through PUBLIC), and the phone remains the only key by design. Non-vacuous: the test applies the captured deployed body FIRST, with the same fixture, and asserts it exposes cnic_front_url and latitude; it also asserts the executed body names no forbidden field and keeps the search_path pin. A coverage guard closes the silent-failure direction: it derives the pre-login read set from the three register pages and auth.ts — resolving camelCase through the store's own mapping — and fails if a field those consumers read is not in the projection (non-vacuous: an injected `myRequest.shopCity` / `request.latitude` / `myRequest.reviewedBy` is reported as uncovered). 12/12 PASS.

The first draft named `phone` as a column (`owner_phone = p_phone OR phone = p_phone`) and the baseline replay passed on BOTH environments — which was not sufficient evidence, because PL/pgSQL resolves column references at execution, not at definition: the first call on production would have raised 'column phone does not exist' and broken the sign-in gate the file exists to protect. The lookup now reads the second spelling through `to_jsonb(sr) ->> 'phone'`, which yields NULL for a key the row type does not have. The ledger that carries the projection agrees byte-for-byte (verify PASS — 193 files, newest 0201, target project bpybjrjenwccowvtrevu). SHARP EDGE, still open by design: the phone is the only key and the deployed API carries no generic rate limit (measured), so a caller who knows a number still receives that number's application stage, and numbers can be walked one at a time. That is the flow's shape — the gate runs before a code is sent and the applicant has no session yet — so narrowing the key or adding a limit is a product decision. features.name: Employees, roles and permissions (RBAC)
rules: Every screen sits behind a permission key declared in the router; a role without it is redirected, not shown a broken screen.
Permissions are enforced in the database (RLS/RPC), not only in the UI.
Role deletion must not orphan employees; the last owner cannot be removed.

Deleting an assigned role SUCCEEDS and revokes the access it provided (0183): every membership pointing at it is cleared to role_id = NULL in the same transaction, so the employees keep their account, membership and history while losing exactly the role's permissions. The screen names how many employees lose the access before confirming.

evidence.proves: RBAC foundation, enforcement, invariants and session lifecycle against QA.
Access UX, role-delete safety and employee status safety on a real browser.

A granted sensitive permission (sales.void) really works and is revoked on change; deleting an assigned role revokes its access from every assigned employee, with no orphaned reference and no bypass from an existing session or a direct RPC.

Invariant D was failing against leaked fixtures rather than a schema property: audit_events.user_id is a NO ACTION foreign key, a suite deleted fixture users without clearing their audit rows, and because one blocked row fails the whole multi-row DELETE the error disappeared into a catch. The shared deleteFixtureUsers helper follows the order delete_my_account already uses and proves the users are gone. Invariant E owner-role exemption is now named AND independently proven — the role comparison must sit inside a NOT_AUTHORIZED refusal — so deleting the owner check fails the test.

Two lanes in this feature were built on RPCs the ledger had already retired, so they could not measure what they claimed and one passed for the wrong reason: `employeeInviteLifecycle` called `deactivate_employee` (no migration defines any such function — only `deactivate_employee_v1` exists) with the failure swallowed by a catch, leaving the SQL beside it doing all the work; and `employeePermissions` called `void_sale_v1` twice, which 0192 revoked with the comment 'The older compatibility endpoint is not used by the application', so the assertion passed on `permission denied` from the grant instead of the identity refusal it names. Both now call the live contract — `deactivate_employee_v1`, and the canonical `void_sale(uuid,text,uuid)` with the payload shape src/lib/db.ts uses — so the refusals come from the authorization checks the tests describe. Found by the RPC contract guard after its fold was corrected to apply every role one statement names.

The retargeted lanes are measured, not merely source-level: the whole integration folder ran against the QA project — 42 files, 493 tests, 0 failures (device-evidence/logs/integration-full-2026-10-15.log), which includes employeeInviteLifecycle — and employeePermissions passed again as part of the 13-file security set on 2026-10-16 (146 tests, exit 0). The identity refusals now come from the live contract (`deactivate_employee_v1`, canonical `void_sale`).

The matrix cannot silently stop describing the system it is evidence for: `tests/unit/securityMatrixCoverage.test.ts` (7/7) reads the RPC→permission mapping back out of the migration that owns it (0192's `guard_operational_request`) and out of the same file's REVOKE of the retired compatibility endpoint, then fails when any guarded, still-reachable RPC is not both CALLED by name in the matrix and asserted with the permission code its guard raises — and separately fails if the matrix stops asserting the guard's refusal text at all. A counted list is deliberately not kept: adding an eighth RPC to the guard changes what the test requires without anyone editing a second file. Non-vacuous, measured: injecting `WHEN 'qa_probe_rpc' THEN 'qa.probe'` into the ledger's CASE mapping fails the guard with "qa_probe_rpc (never called in the matrix)"; the migration file was reverted byte-clean (`git status` empty for `supabase/migrations/`) and replay/schema guards re-run green (23/23).

The per-role backend matrix the staging checklist recorded as never run is now measured in one tenant, on the same consequential RPCs: customers.create is the shop-floor permission (owner, admin, manager and employee all pass the guard), sales.void passes for owner/admin/manager and is refused for the employee with `missing permission sales.void`, inventory.adjust and employees.manage pass for the owner only, and products.delete is refused for every non-owner. An admin whose role carries one unrelated permission is refused exactly like an employee, so `admin` is a role and not the implicit set `owner` is. Refusals are asserted as the guard's own text and allows as the ABSENCE of it, so a call that never reached the guard cannot read as an allow. Non-vacuous, measured: granting sales.void to the employee role flips exactly the employee assertion ("employee was NOT refused void_sale: expected 'NOT_AUTHORIZED: record branch access …' to contain 'missing permission sales.void'"). The same file covers the direct-API bypass (anon RPC and anon reads refused; an employee cannot INSERT into customer_payments/sales or grant itself a permission through user_permissions, with the permission set and row count re-measured after the refusal) and the sensitive-field read gate (zero customers/companies/product_variants rows without the permission, real rows for the owner as the control).

risks: src/lib/accessModel.ts and permissionLabels.ts are Tier-2 paths: touching them forces the full gate.
securityMatrix creates its own personas and roles in the QA tenant with unique names and removes them; the QA baseline check is the independent proof it leaves nothing behind.

features.name: Shop/branch scope and tenant isolation
rules: Every row is shop-scoped; a shop can never read or write another shop's rows.
RLS policies on shop-scoped tables are the boundary — the client never decides it.
Branch context switches must reset cached state (no cross-branch leakage).
A branch on this tenant is identified by its own branch id, not by the tenant id that owns it.

Removing a branch ARCHIVES it. `archive_operating_branch` is the only removal path — owner-only, tenant-scoped, reason required, refusing MAIN_BRANCH / LAST_BRANCH / BRANCH_HAS_STAFF, keeping every record and writing a `branch_archived` audit row with `historyPreserved: true`. The erase path (`delete_branch`, `purge_branch_data`, `purge_shop_data`) is revoked from `authenticated` and no screen may call it — `tests/unit/rpcContractGuard.test.ts` fails on any client or lane call to a function the ledger revokes.
Unknown branch facts (counts, scope, place) must never be rendered as if they were empty or absent.

evidence.proves: Two live cross-tenant leaks (audit_events SELECT, app_settings read/write) were closed by migrations 0181/0182 and re-verified with a real JWT.

Shop-scoped stores, cart, nav and cache are cleared on a same-tenant branch switch; offline queue now records the tenant/userId/branchId it was created under and refuses to replay work whose original context no longer matches the confirmed device context; the sync lock is released in a finally so an unexpected localStorage/network throw cannot wedge it; unknown branch counts are rendered as neutral instead of as empty.

The suite asserted a direct authenticated INSERT into sales, which 0195 revoked precisely so a caller cannot choose its own branch. It now creates records through create_sale and proves the stamp follows the actor scope (a warehouse-scoped employee is stamped warehouse, not the tenant default), that the direct ledger write and a cross-tenant write are refused and persist nothing, and that reads follow the branch being WORKED IN — one branch at a time, re-scoped by set_active_branch, with an unheld branch not switchable.

The branch-pin read was asserted against the pre-0188 model, where a second TENANT stood in for another branch and the list was keyed on shop_id. get_my_branches() returns real branches of the tenant being worked in, and a pin is written to the branches row. The rewritten lane proves the pin travels with a sibling branch, that an un-pinned branch reports null rather than 0/0, and that another tenant branch is neither listed nor writable by id.

The branch half of DeleteTargetSheet now archives instead of erasing. It calls archiveBranch → archive_operating_branch, refuses to leave the reason step without a reason, reads the `archived: {name, fallbackName}` payload the archive path actually returns (it used to expect a `deleted` shape nothing returns), and answers every refusal the archive can raise — main_branch, last_branch, has_staff, not_found, denied, not_authenticated — with a key that exists in both EN and UR. The branch copy no longer claims records are deleted in either language, while the account half still says it erases, because it does. Non-vacuous: a legacy deleteBranch call, an '…will be deleted' string, or a missing refusal key each fail the guard (4 failures, measured).

The RPC permission contract between the source and the migration ledger is now asserted, not read by hand: every statically named supabase.rpc / scopedRpc call under src/ must resolve to a function `authenticated` can execute as the ledger leaves it, the same for every lane call through execRpcAsUser, and a client call into a function the ledger revokes fails with the statement that retired it. The fold reads ledger order, an explicit GRANT followed by REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC keeping the grant, and DROP discarding the ACL while CREATE OR REPLACE keeps it. Measured at this revision (191 migrations folded into 182 functions): 65 client call names across 76 call sites in 16 files, 214 lane calls in 20 files, 2 unresolved names both accounted for, and 3 functions the ledger keeps server-only (delete_branch, mint_barcode, marketplace_distance_km). Non-vacuous, measured: injecting the 77e5bc66 regression (a supabase.rpc("delete_branch") call), a migration that revokes create_sale, a lane calling a revoked RPC, an unresolved name, a second unresolved name behind an existing exemption, a missing PUBLIC-default entry and an unevidenced ledger gap each produce the expected failure (14/14 in the file, including a real capture: the first run flagged tests/integration/employeeInviteLifecycle.test.ts calling deactivate_employee, which no migration defines).

The fold was checked against the deployed catalogs read-only rather than against itself, and corrected where it disagreed. Six functions were measured with has_function_privilege (backups/get-my-shop-request-acl-2026-10-13.log): for the five the ledger speaks about, the model now reproduces the deployment exactly per role (archive_operating_branch false/true, delete_branch false/false, get_my_shops false/true, insert_shop_request true/true, lookup_user_by_phone true/true) — a comparison that caught a real modelling bug, because a statement naming PUBLIC, anon and authenticated was applying only the first role it matched. That bug had been reading the retired void_sale_v1 as still granted to authenticated and therefore hid two lane call sites on it (see employees-roles). The sixth function, get_my_shop_request, was the gap case at the time of that probe. 0200 has since written its CREATE and its two grants into the ledger, so the fold and the deployment now agree for all six measured functions (6/6) and LEDGER_GAPS is empty; the rule that refuses a gap the ledger has outgrown is kept non-vacuous, so re-adding that exemption fails rather than quietly weakening the check (see registration-shop-requests).

The branch half of tests/integration/accountDeletion.test.ts was built on the revoked `delete_branch`, so it could not measure anything. It now proves the surviving contract with `archive_operating_branch`: BRANCH_HAS_STAFF while a person is still scoped to the branch, the archive that follows once they are moved (fallback_branch_id = the surviving branch, the working-context row reassigned to it, is_active = false, the branch row and the person's login still present), the MAIN_BRANCH refusal, and the untouched sibling branch, shop and tenant-level record. The account-deletion half — register, be approved, delete the number, register the same number again with nothing left behind — is unchanged.

The tenant/branch boundaries were re-measured against the live QA project on 2026-10-16 as one 13-file security set (146 tests, exit 0, EnvGuard verified bpybjrjenwccowvtrevu): tenantBoundarySweep (all four views read as a real authenticated session, `tenants` 1 own / 0 foreign after 0206), branchScopeEnforcement (12 tests: branch stamping, cross-branch write refusal, one-branch-at-a-time reads, an empty or NULL non-owner scope refused), variantIsolation (cost_price hidden from the employee projection and the base table admin-only) and securityMatrix (a write addressed to a sibling branch refused for a branch-scoped manager and accepted for the owner; a member's `sales` read restricted to the branch being worked in; the read gate returning zero customers/companies/product_variants rows without the permission, with the owner's real rows as the non-vacuity control).

The browser-driven leg of branch removal is now measured, not blocked: `tests/e2e/branchRemoval.spec.ts` drives the real screen against the real database — the main branch offers no archive action, the confirmation names the branch and states the real consequence (history preserved), the confirm button is DISABLED until a reason is typed, the owner's archive succeeds and the success toast agrees with the rows (`is_active = false`, the branch row still present, the main branch and the `shops` row untouched), and an employee is shown no archive surface at all. The reload/resume half is measured by `tests/e2e/sessionRefresh.spec.ts`: the owner's customer data and the permission-gated settings route are the same before, after `page.reload()` and after a NEW page in the same profile, and the branch switched through the app's own switcher (the real `set_active_branch`) survives both — asserted in `user_active_shops.branch_id` AND in the switcher's `aria-selected` row. Each lane deletes its own branch by id and reads back 0 rows left behind. Non-vacuity: the first run of `branchRemoval` failed on a selector that could not match the shared `Input` (a bare <input> with no `type`), and `sessionRefresh`'s branch test failed on a precondition `UPDATE` that matched 0 rows because `user_active_shops` had no row for that user — both were real failure modes the lanes surfaced, fixed, and re-run green.

risks: app_settings was missing from BUSINESS_TABLES in scripts/dev/lib.mjs when 0182 was found — verify cleanup coverage when adding a new shop-scoped table.

This record's 2026-10-06 caveat that 0188–0195 were local and unapplied is superseded: they are in the QA ledger (198 files / 198 rows, hashes matching) and the tenant/branch boundaries above are measured against the live project. The browser-driven branch-removal flow it also named was measured on 2026-10-16 (`tests/e2e/branchRemoval.spec.ts`, `sessionRefresh.spec.ts`), so no leg of this record is `BLOCKED` any more — see device-evidence/session-and-branch-removal-live-2026-10-16.md.
The marketplace enablement keeps its tenant-level storage while the UI presents it beside one branch; that mismatch is documented, not resolved by this patch.

features.name: Companies directory (suppliers/manufacturers)
rules: A company is a prerequisite entity: products and purchases link to one.

evidence.proves: Company CRUD works under admin full access and stays tenant-scoped.

features.name: Products, variants, packs and barcodes
rules: One product = one card per pack variant; price and stock live on the variant, not the product.
Deleting a product is a destructive action: refused or archived, never a silent data loss.

evidence.proves: Price traceability holds against QA; pack-size and draft logic are unit-locked.
Opening stock entered in the product form reaches inventory correctly in a browser.

risks: Path matches the Tier-2 keyword list (products/inventory wording), so changes here force the full gate.

features.name: Inventory adjustments, movements and reorder
rules: Stock only moves through adjust_stock or a sale/purchase/return — never by writing quantity directly.
Every movement keeps its reason and actor for history.

evidence.proves: Inventory integrity (stock never double-restored by a void after a return, derived product rollup equals its active variants) against QA. Each branch-owned row states its own branch, the suite proves the branch-scope trigger is still enabled and still refuses a return addressed to a nonexistent branch, and cleanup removes every row it writes — the previous version swallowed its cleanup errors and left a sale and a sale_item behind after every run.

risks: The word 'inventory' in a path is Tier-2 — treat genuinely.

features.name: Low-stock thresholds and alert settings
rules: Threshold per product, default per shop; alerts derive from stock minus threshold, never a stored copy.
Settings rows are shop-scoped; another shop must not read or write them.

evidence.proves: app_settings was readable and writable across tenants; migration 0182 scoped both, re-verified with two real tenants.
Threshold math and alert derivation are unit-locked.

The 0182 product claim is unchanged; the lane needed a fixture correction, not a product change. get_stock_alert_settings authorizes products.view (0157) and after 0195 that resolves through has_effective_permission plus a non-null current_branch_id, so the seeded employee — membership role_id NULL, no branch scope — was refused for reasons unrelated to app_settings. The lane now uses its own employee holding the tenant real stock role and a real branch, and all six isolation assertions still hold.

features.name: Purchases and supplier ordering
rules: A purchase increases stock and creates a supplier payable in one transaction; partial payment is allowed.

evidence.proves: Purchase totals and supplier payable reconcile against QA. Recording the same payment twice must be idempotent (reentrancy guard).

features.name: Notifications
rules: A notification belongs to the business that posted it AND names the operating branch it happened in (0197): the branch comes from the record itself where the record has one (a sale, a purchase, the sale a return came from), else from the branch the actor was working in. Stamped on insert only, never rewritten by a later update.

Reads are bounded twice: by business membership (`my_shop_ids`, 0168) and by branch scope (`notification_branch_visible`, 0197 — NULL scope for an owner, the member's own branches otherwise). A member scoped to one branch cannot read another's rows.

A row the database never attributed (`branch_id IS NULL`) stays readable to the whole business and belongs to no branch tab: existing history is never re-attributed to a branch it may never have happened in.
The branch tabs filter by `branch_id`. `shop_id` is the business and `branch_id` is the operating branch — different id spaces, never interchangeable.
Mark-read is optimistic but rolls back on a failed server write, so a network failure cannot leave rows marked read; from a branch tab it marks that branch's rows only, not every branch's.

evidence.proves: Notification scoping and unread behaviour are asserted against the persisted/notifications contract.

The branch tabs read branch ids: each tab shows its own branch's rows and no other's, the all-branches view names the branch on each attributed row, an unattributed row is shown there and claimed by no branch, and marking read from a tab touches that branch only. Non-vacuous: restoring the old `shop_id === branch.id` comparison fails both languages.

risks: Branch scope is enforced by RLS (`notification_branch_visible`) and asserted at the UI-contract level by a mocked-transport lane; the two have not been exercised together against the live database in one automated run (the live policy was read back from pg_policies after 0197 was applied, and the column is present with 0 of the existing rows attributed — none were re-attributed).

A branch's responsible person (0196) reads that branch's rows when their branch scope covers it, but the client-side persona filter still shows a non-owner only the kinds an employee may see, so a responsible person who is not an owner/admin does not see that branch's sales in the bell. That rule was left as it was rather than widened without the owner's decision.
The client create path still sends no branch id and lets the database stamp it; if a caller ever passes one, the insert policy refuses a branch outside the caller's scope rather than trusting it.

The audit read is gated on has_effective_permission(activity.view) AND tenant_id = current_shop_id() plus branch scope, so a fixture row inserted with no tenant attribution is invisible to its own admin — that, not a missing permission, is what made the lane red (the same call returns 452 rows, so the admin does hold activity.view). The fixture now attributes both rows and the negative control is unchanged: another shop history stays unreadable.

features.name: Offline queue and sync
rules: A queued write is replayed once, in order, and never duplicated.

An offline write records the tenant/userId/branchId it was created under and is refused if the confirmed device context no longer matches.
The sync lock is released in a finally, so an unexpected localStorage or network throw cannot wedge the queue.

evidence.proves: Cache ownership is per-shop, so a shop switch cannot serve another shop's cache.
The offline queue is ownership-aware, retains legacy unowned work instead of guessing a branch, preserves work queued during an in-flight sync, and the sync lock is released in a finally.
The offline update_note replay wrote sales.note. It now writes notes, the only column the grant permits, so a queued note can no longer be replayed into a column that does not exist.

features.name: Farmer marketplace listing (owner side)
rules: A product appears to a buyer only when its own listing switch AND the branch's switch are on, the branch has a pinned location, the product and pack are active, and the pack has stock and a price above zero.

A branch is eligible only when it is within the radius the SEARCHER chose. The owner sets a location and a switch and no distance at all: 0187 dropped shops.marketplace_radius_km, so there is one radius and it cannot be overridden by either side.
Nearest eligible branch first, with price then name breaking ties deterministically. A product carried by two branches is two rows.
The public read contract is a fixed 20-column projection readable anonymously; base tables stay unreachable to anon and no write through the contract is possible.
The Owner App is the single source of truth: the contract is a view over live rows, so unlisting, archiving and price or stock changes take effect on the next read with no propagation step.

Turning a branch's switch on is refused when the branch has no location. The switch is the whole owner-side decision — turning it off is accepted like turning it on, and there is no distance for it to keep.

In this checkout the marketplace enablement is still stored on the tenant row, while the UI presents one branch-level-looking switch beside a chosen branch. This checkout documents that mismatch and keeps the listing contract judged against the tenant RPC, not against the new branch-id reality; the remaining work item is tracked separately and is not asserted live here.

evidence.proves: 28 integration tests on the real QA project prove the anonymous boundary (four base tables refused, view read-only, settings writer refused), the exact 20-column allowlist, every eligibility rule, the farmer's radius enforced in both directions with no owner-side setting touched, nearest-first ordering, owner-only authority for the switch, that the writer takes exactly two arguments (a stale third-argument call fails), and that get_my_branches carries the switch and no distance.

17 guard tests fail on a projected forbidden column under any alias, on a renamed or disclosed allowlist entry and on SELECT *, and fail if the search rule stops bounding distance by the farmer's radius or reads a branch-side distance again (0187). Proven non-vacuous by injecting v.cost_price and by smuggling LEAST(v_radius, s.marketplace_radius_km) back into the search rule and watching each mutation get caught. The migration self-proof block refuses to apply on the same conditions.

The browser lane drives both switches through the real screens: the product tick is stored with its listing moment, a listed product opens listed and an unrelated save does not unlist it, and unticking it unlists and clears the moment; the branch switch saves, makes a listed product reachable through the public contract, and turning the branch off removes it again. The read-back assertion was proven non-vacuous by reintroducing the read-path defect and watching the lane fail. A third test switches the app to Urdu and proves both new controls are announced in Urdu, no English copy is left on either card, and the owner-side distance row is gone in every language.

risks: The public surface is a projection, not a table: adding a column to the view's SELECT or relaxing its WHERE changes what is public. The guard catches forbidden names, but a deliberately added column still needs its own decision - see FARMER_MARKETPLACE_INTEGRATION.md section 7.
Archive is products.is_active = false (there is no products.deleted_at); a future hard-delete path would bypass the view's archive rule and needs to re-check the eligibility chain.

features.name: Production error reporting and release timeline
rules: Off is off: an unconfigured reporter returns enabled:false with a reason and installs no handler, because a monitoring path that silently drops everything reads as coverage.

Nothing a customer typed leaves the browser: request, user, extra, breadcrumbs, modules and server_name are removed, contexts are limited to browser/os/runtime, and every surviving string has e-mails, phone-shaped digit runs and tokens redacted.
Every event names the commit the bundle was built from, so an error can be tied to a deploy; the release timeline records only deploys whose workflow concluded success.
The private record in client_error_events is unchanged: write-only for clients, readable by the service role and by nobody else.

evidence.proves: A real built bundle reported an uncaught error and an unhandled rejection to a local ingest: one event envelope each, release agrishop-app@testsha123, environment staging, phone and e-mail and token redacted, uuid and timestamp preserved, and no user, request, breadcrumbs, ip_address or user_agent in the payload.

Gating, redaction, release resolution, the release-marker plan and the source-scan wiring rules are locked by guards, including a control proving the raw payload really carried the values that were redacted.
Production notification is NOT proven: no Sentry project, DSN or SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN exists yet, so no alert has ever fired from production and no real deploy has been recorded on the timeline.

risks: Until VITE_SENTRY_DSN is set for the production Vercel environment, the alert path is disabled by design: errors are still recorded in client_error_events and nobody is notified.
Session envelopes were measured carrying user_agent and ip_address:{{auto}}; the BrowserSession integration is filtered out and a guard pins that filter.
